preregistration_text.text: (3) MEASURES, per pair and c != 0 (D-156 means over draws; seed-mean flags per draw, as D-351 (2)): the Gaussian detector's false-alarm share fp / (fp + tn) and sensitivity; the direct detector's (D-264, no Gaussian assumption) the same; P-A1.3's log(realised/predicted) (unfloored, as the verdict line). TAIL STATISTIC per pair (independent of any attack): tau = (q99(E post scores) - m) / s - Phi^-1(0.99), m and s the mean and SD (ddof 0, as D-346 (2)(b)) of the same scores, per draw and seed, D-156 mean; tau > 0 means an upper tail heavier than Gaussian at the 1% level. (4) READING, fixed now: the shared-heavy-tail account is SUPPORTED only if all four hold: (a) at least 80% of the Gaussian detector's pooled false alarms (sum over pairs and c of the D-156 mean fp) fall at c < 0; (b) the direct detector's pooled false-alarm rate at c < 0 is below the Gaussian detector's; (c) tau > 0 in at least 7 of the 9 pairs; (d) across the nine pairs the Spearman correlation between tau and the pair's mean log(realised/predicted) over c < 0 is positive (reported with n = 9; no significance claimed). Otherwise NOT SUPPORTED, with each part's value. Either way no A1 verdict changes (D-353 stands); the result informs how C2, C5 and C6 are worded.

reading.b: the direct detector's pooled false-alarm rate at c < 0 strictly below the Gaussian detector's
reading.a_b_comparison: exact, as fractions of integer totals (fp and tn summed over the pairs, the c set and draws 1..; every pair has the same draws, so these are the ratios of the summed D-156 mean counts)
reading.d: Spearman correlation (scipy.stats.spearmanr, average ranks) > 0 (strict), n = 9, no p-value

tail.scores: the post scores at c = 0 of the draw's E (1000 negatives), per draw and seed
tail.summary: per draw the seed mean; the D-156 mean over draws 1..

bootstrap_of_the_anchor.role: only to reproduce the pooled record's P-A1.4 blocks; no by-c interval

draws_npz.rows: <pair>|q99 and <pair>|tau: draw index (0 the frozen split) x seeds in config order

choices: (a) Per pair and c, the false-alarm share is the D-156 mean fp over the D-156 mean fp + tn (draws 1.., the frozen split beside), and the sensitivity the D-156 mean tp over tp + fn: the ratio of the means, D-353's 'D-156 mean fp of fp + tn per draw' and D-255's pooled form (healthcheck_summary_d156.pooled_counts, pooled_from_mean_counts). With one cell per pair, c and draw it equals the share of the draws in the realised negative class that are flagged. Undefined (None) when no draw has the cell in that class.

(b) Part (a): the share is the sum over the nine pairs and the five c < 0 of the Gaussian D-156 mean fp over the same sum over every c != 0 (the latter is the P-A1.4 verdict line's mean fp, reproduced from the pooled record). With no false alarm at all the share is undefined and the part does not hold.

(c) Part (b): each detector's pooled false-alarm rate at c < 0 is fp / (fp + tn) of the D-156 mean counts summed over the nine pairs and the five c < 0 (D-255's pooled form, as P-A1.4's specificity is formed); 'below' is strict; an undefined rate (no negative-class cell at c < 0) makes the part not hold.

(d) The tail statistic: per draw d and seed s, x the post scores at c = 0 of E_d (phase3_a1_predictions.setup's scores, unchanged: SC['post']['pool'][E]); m = x.mean(axis=0), s = x.std(axis=0) (ddof 0) exactly as phase3_a1_predictions.build forms them and required equal to its m and s bit for bit; q99 = numpy.quantile(x, 0.99, axis=0) in float64 with numpy's default linear interpolation (the implementer's choice, recorded); tau = (q99 - m) / s - scipy.stats.norm.ppf(0.99). Per draw the seed mean, then the D-156 mean over draws 1.. (band and frozen split beside). Part (c) compares the D-156 mean with 0 strictly; a pair with no finite tau does not count.

(e) Part (d): the pair's mean of the signed log(realised/predicted) over its five c < 0 cells, realised and predicted the verdict line's (phase3_a1_pooled.cell_rows, white-box, unfloored). A zero prediction gives +inf (a miss, D-322 (4)), ranked highest (recorded as None with the count; D-353: no cell was predicted zero). The Spearman correlation is scipy.stats.spearmanr (average ranks for ties); 'positive' is > 0; an undefined correlation (a constant vector, or a pair with no finite tau) is not positive. No p-value is computed (D-370 (4): no significance claimed).

(f) White-box only (D-370 (2): the white-box A1 records; D-346 (2)(g)); c != 0 scored, c = 0 not used for the false alarms; the per-draw unit is the seed-mean flag (D-351 (2)); the transfer variant is not read.

(g) Binding: the records' A1 code block must equal this tree's file for file (the tail statistic re-scores the caches through it, so 'unchanged' is checked, not assumed), src/phase3_a1.py and src/phase3_a1_predictions.py the reviewed blobs, src/phase3_a1_pooled.py and src/healthcheck_summary_d156.py the D-353 record's (PINNED_SHA256); the pooled record is D-353's by sha256 when the records are results/'s.

(h) FIX ROUND (three reviews of 94e7dc6/b6b7594; rules (a)-(g) unchanged): parts (a) and (b) are compared exactly, as fractions of integer totals (fp and tn summed over the nine pairs, the c set and draws 1..): (a) 5 j >= 4 k with j, k the Gaussian fp totals at c < 0 and at every c != 0; (b) the direct fp / (fp + tn) below the Gaussian's as fractions. Every pair has the same draws, so these are exactly the ratios of the summed D-156 mean counts of (b) and (c) above, without their floating-point sums.

(i) The q99 estimator's offset, recorded, not corrected (D-370 (3) fixed tau): numpy's linear q99 of |E| = 1000 scores, standardised by the sample m and s, runs low under a Gaussian null (the review's figure: about 0.02), so 'tau > 0' means an upper tail heavier than Gaussian by about that much. The record's tail_statistic_gaussian_null_beside gives the same estimator's mean tau over standard-normal samples of 1000 (GAUSS_NULL: count and seed) with its Monte Carlo standard error, beside only.

(j) Dtypes, recorded per pair (tail_statistic.per_pair.<pair>.dtypes): m and s are computed in the post scores' own dtype exactly as build computes them (numpy's mean and std of that array); q99 on the same scores cast to float64; tau in float64. No computation changes with the dtype.

(k) Beside part (d), not in the reading: the pair's mean log(realised/predicted) over c < 0 with the prediction floored per seed at 1/|E| (the realised side's floor; the pooled record's floored prediction, D-346 (2)(e)); and D-177's accuracy line (phase3_a1.accuracy, unfloored: n cells, share within x1.5, median |log|) per c, per pair over c < 0 and over c > 0, and pooled over each c set.
